questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: The opening infertility definition uses failure to conceive after ____ of unprotected intercourse.
questions.exp: The general definition is one year; the following age table shortens the investigation interval.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: Match female age with the source's waiting period: A) <35 B) ≥35 C) >45; 1) 3 months 2) 1 year 3) 6 months.
questions.exp: These are the source-table intervals. In clinical practice, women over 40 generally merit prompt evaluation rather than waiting for the >45 row.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: A woman previously conceived but miscarried and now cannot conceive. Which type fits the definition here?
opts: Neither, because a live birth is required
questions.exp: Any previous conception, irrespective of outcome, distinguishes secondary from primary infertility.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: Primary infertility means the female partner has ____.
opts: Never delivered a live infant despite prior conception
questions.exp: The definition depends on conception, not the outcome of a pregnancy.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: In the source's cause list, male-factor contribution is ____ while male factors alone account for ____.
questions.exp: The contribution including combined causes is higher than the male-only percentage.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: The source writes a descending female-factor range '40–35%'; the separate unexplained-infertility figure is ____.
questions.exp: Magnified review confirms the unusual handwritten 40–35% range, not 40–55%. Do not silently normalise that annotation; the unexplained figure is clearly 10%.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: Match 1) Fecundability 2) Fecundity with A) Probability of live birth in a cycle B) Probability of conception in a cycle.
questions.exp: Conception and live-birth probabilities are distinct endpoints.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: The fecundability figure written for the first cycle after marriage is ____.
questions.exp: The conception-probability column gives 20%.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: Source-check: the adjacent table gives fecundability 20% but live-birth fecundity 50% for the same cycle. What is the problem?
opts: Live-birth probability must be multiplied by two before comparing the values
The two percentages can be compared directly without a common denominator
Fecundability counts only pregnancies after three failed treatment cycles
For the same cohort and cycle, live births cannot exceed conceptions
questions.exp: Retain the definitions but recognise the incompatible percentages; do not memorise 50% as a valid linked live-birth probability.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: Match initial tests: 1) Male factor 2) Ovulation 3) Tubal patency with A) HSG days 7–10 B) Semen analysis C) Luteal progesterone.
questions.exp: The source lists all three before diagnosing unexplained infertility.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: The male-infertility chapter writes progesterone on day ____, while the earlier chapter uses day 21. What timing principle reconciles the examples?
opts: 22; sample about a week before the expected period
3; always use the first day of bleeding
questions.exp: Day 21/22 are illustrative luteal dates; the clinically meaningful timing is about seven days before menstruation.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: Semen analysis, ovulation assessment and HSG are all normal. Which diagnosis and treatment are shown?
questions.exp: Normal basic investigations lead to the unexplained-infertility branch in the notes.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: For a female partner aged ≥35, which reserve test is added in this opening work-up?
questions.exp: The additional line specifies ovarian reserve testing with serum AMH.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: The commonest male-infertility cause in the chapter is abnormal spermatogenesis due to ____ causes.
questions.exp: The first male-cause line links testicular dysfunction to gonadal failure and gives Klinefelter as an example.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: The commonest reversible male-infertility cause named is ____.
opts: Complete congenital bilateral absence of the vas
questions.exp: Varicocele is explicitly distinguished from the commonest overall testicular category.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: A couple asks about increasing paternal age. Which sperm change is highlighted?
opts: Inevitable CFTR mutation in every sperm
questions.exp: The age note points to structural and chromosomal defects, not improved semen quality.

questions.sec: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.unit: Infertility definitions, evaluation and male causes
questions.q: The sperm-quality monitoring test named before IVF is ____.
questions.exp: The source names DNA fragmentation testing before IVF; this is a source-specific statement, not a requirement for every couple.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The recommended abstinence interval for semen collection is typically ____ within an acceptable ____ range.
questions.exp: The page specifies three days, with two to seven as the range.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Match collection errors: 1) <2 days abstinence 2) >7 days abstinence with A) Falsely high dead-sperm concentration B) Falsely low sperm concentration.
questions.exp: Short abstinence can lower concentration; prolonged abstinence increases dead-sperm representation.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: A semen sample should reach the laboratory within ____.
questions.exp: The source sets a one-hour transport interval.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Semen analysis is performed after liquefaction, normally taking ____ in these notes.
questions.exp: The liquefaction interval is distinct from the one-hour transport limit.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Which collection method matches the chapter's instructions?
opts: Collection in a routine latex condom
A cervical postcoital smear instead of semen
questions.exp: The source specifies a sterile container and explicitly excludes latex condoms.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Match epididymal function: 1) Proximal end 2) Distal end with A) Motility B) Maturity.
questions.exp: The maturity/motility lines place maturation proximally and motility distally.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The semen-reference table is labelled WHO ____ and gives minimum volume ____.
questions.exp: These are the source table's year label and volume value; reference limits do not by themselves define fertility.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The pH minimum in the semen table is ____.
questions.exp: The table lists 7.2 in the pH row.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: No semen is produced at ejaculation. Which term is correct?
questions.exp: Aspermia is absence of semen; azoospermia is absence of sperm in semen.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The lower sperm-concentration reference in the table is ____ million/mL.
questions.exp: Sixteen is the concentration limit; 39 is total sperm number per ejaculate.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Semen concentration is 12 million/mL. Which concentration term applies under the notes' definitions?
questions.exp: Oligospermia is below 16 million/mL; the severe group is below 5 million/mL.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Severe oligospermia is defined here as ____ million/mL.
questions.exp: The severe threshold is less than five, not merely below the reference limit of sixteen.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Severe oligospermia or azoospermia prompts which further assessment in the table?
opts: Semen culture and antibiotics alone before any hormonal assessment
Repeat morphology alone, deferring all endocrine and genetic assessment
Hormonal and genetic assessment, including Klinefelter evaluation
Fructose measurement alone, assuming a distal obstructive cause
questions.exp: The bracket links severe oligospermia and azoospermia to hormonal/genetic work-up.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The minimum normal morphology reference is ____ using strict ____ criteria.
questions.exp: Four percent and strict Tygerberg criteria belong to the morphology row; the IUI block later uses a different historical figure.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The main abnormality is an excess of morphologically abnormal sperm. Which term fits?
questions.exp: Teratozoospermia concerns form, not concentration or movement.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Minimum total motility and progressive motility are respectively ____.
questions.exp: Total movement includes non-progressive movement and therefore exceeds progressive motility.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Motility is reduced without proof that sperm are dead. Which term is appropriate?
questions.exp: Motility and viability are separate; immobile sperm may still be alive.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The semen viability reference is ____; increased nonviable sperm is termed ____.
questions.exp: Viability is not interchangeable with motility or morphology.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The minimum total sperm number is ____ per ejaculate.
questions.exp: Total number per ejaculate is a different measure from concentration per millilitre.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Match 1) Concentration 2) Morphology 3) Total number with A) 4% B) 39 million/ejaculate C) 16 million/mL.
questions.exp: The units prevent mixing percentages, concentrations and total counts.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The source ranks the importance of semen parameters as ____.
questions.exp: This is the source's teaching hierarchy, not a stand-alone clinical prognostic rule.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The two semen parameters described as unchanged from 2010 to 2022 are ____.
questions.exp: The two-item note follows the parameter hierarchy.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: The karyotype named for Klinefelter-associated azoospermia is ____.
questions.exp: The common-cause line gives 47XXY, with an extra X chromosome.

questions.sec: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.unit: Semen collection and reference-parameter table
questions.q: Azoospermia is accompanied by congenital absence of both vasa and seminal-vesicle abnormalities. Which gene is named?
questions.exp: Cystic fibrosis/CFTR-related absence is the second common-cause example; anatomy can vary and the source is simplified.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Infertility, recurrent sinusitis and recurrent chest infection from bronchiectasis suggest which cause of asthenospermia?
questions.exp: The asthenospermia block links respiratory ciliary dysfunction with sperm immotility.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: The non-syndromic exposure listed beside immotile cilia syndrome as a cause of asthenospermia is ____.
opts: DES exposure in the female partner
A low-estrogen pill in the partner
questions.exp: Smoking appears both in this list and in the OATS associations.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Young syndrome causes thick mucus blocking the nose, bronchi and vas deferens. Which presentation is listed?
opts: Hot flushes, high FSH and low AMH
Cyclical pain, urinary retention and haematocolpos
questions.exp: Young syndrome is a mucus-obstructive comparison beside the immotile-cilia cause.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: OATS expands to oligospermia plus ____ plus ____.
questions.exp: OATS combines low concentration, poor movement and abnormal morphology.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: The two associations named for OATS are ____.
questions.exp: These are the two exposures/conditions immediately below the OATS expansion.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: The Klinefelter incidence range written here is ____ pregnancies.
questions.exp: The source gives a range per thousand pregnancies.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: A tall infertile man has long limbs, gynaecomastia and small hypoplastic testes. Which diagnosis fits?
opts: Congenital absence of vas with normal testes only
Complete AIS in a phenotypic female
questions.exp: This is the characteristic phenotype listed under 47XXY.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Which is NOT in the source's increased-tumour-risk list for Klinefelter syndrome?
questions.exp: The three listed risks are breast cancer, NHL and extragonadal germ-cell tumours.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: The notes additionally describe ____ lifespan and ____ IQ in Klinefelter syndrome.
questions.exp: These are source annotations, not universal traits; cognitive profiles and life expectancy vary between individuals.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: The pictured bead-based instrument used to estimate testicular size is the ____.
questions.exp: The illustration is labelled Prader orchidometer and measures testis size.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Spermatogenesis begins at ____ and occurs in ____.
questions.exp: The page separately states pubertal onset and depicts the seminiferous-tubule site.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Match gonadotropins: 1) FSH 2) LH with A) Leydig cells B) Sertoli cells.
questions.exp: The hypothalamic-pituitary diagram sends FSH to Sertoli and LH to Leydig cells.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Sertoli cells release ____ while Leydig cells release ____.
questions.exp: Inhibin B feeds back to FSH; testosterone supports spermatogenesis and feeds back centrally.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: I) Inhibin B inhibits FSH through feedback. II) Testosterone contributes to spermatogenesis and negative central feedback.
questions.exp: Both feedback loops are shown with dashed inhibitory arrows in the diagram.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Arrange the main sperm passage route: A) Vas deferens B) Testis C) Epididymis D) Ejaculatory duct.
questions.exp: Sperm leave the testis, mature in the epididymis and pass through the vas to the ejaculatory duct.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Seminal-vesicle secretion is rich in ____ and forms a ____ component of semen.
questions.exp: The vesicles contribute fructose-rich fluid, not sperm production.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: The gland also called Cowper's is the ____ gland.
questions.exp: The pathway diagram labels bulbourethral/Cowper's gland as an additional secretory source.

questions.sec: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.unit: Asthenospermia, Klinefelter and sperm pathway
questions.q: Which structure in the pathway diagram produces sperm rather than adding secretions or transporting them?
questions.exp: The testis performs spermatogenesis; the others contribute fluid or passage.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Match 1) Pretesticular 2) Testicular 3) Post-testicular with A) Testis B) Hypothalamus/pituitary C) Epididymis/vas/ejaculatory tract.
questions.exp: The source classifies dysfunction by central control, sperm production and passage.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: I) Post-testicular organs are necessary for sperm passage. II) They are the site of spermatogenesis.
questions.exp: The page explicitly says necessary for passage, not necessary for spermatogenesis.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Prostatic enzymes are responsible for semen ____.
questions.exp: The semen-source list assigns liquefaction to prostatic enzymes.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: The bulbourethral gland adds secretion at the time of ____.
questions.exp: This timing is given in the third semen-source bullet.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: A first semen analysis shows azoospermia. Before committing to an aetiological diagnosis, what is the next step?
opts: Diagnose Klinefelter solely from one sample
questions.exp: The algorithm first repeats the semen analysis to confirm azoospermia.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: The source's repeat-semen interval is ideally ____ and at minimum ____.
questions.exp: Both intervals are boxed beside repeat semen analysis.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Confirmed azoospermia is followed by measurement of ____.
questions.exp: The three-hormone panel precedes the low, high and normal FSH branches.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Azoospermia with low FSH and low testosterone points to which level?
questions.exp: Low gonadotropins and low gonadal hormone suggest a pretesticular central cause.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Which is NOT in the central hypogonadotropic-cause list?
questions.exp: Mumps orchitis is in the testicular branch, not the central branch.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Hyperprolactinaemia suppresses ____ in the central azoospermia pathway.
questions.exp: The source attributes its central effect to inhibition of GnRH.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Arrange the chronic-hypothyroidism mechanism: A) Raised TRH B) Low T3 C) Raised TSH and prolactin.
questions.exp: Low thyroid hormone increases TRH, which stimulates both TSH and prolactin.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Confirmed azoospermia with high FSH and low testosterone suggests ____.
opts: Unexplained infertility with all tests normal
Purely obstructive azoospermia with normal gonadal function
questions.exp: Failed testicular function reduces testosterone and raises gonadotropins.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Which is outside the source's testicular-failure example list?
questions.exp: Vasectomy obstructs the pathway; the testicular list also includes heat exposure in miners.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: The occupational example linked to testicular heat exposure is ____.
questions.exp: The notes specifically give miners as the heat-exposure example.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Azoospermia with normal FSH and normal testosterone enters which source algorithm branch?
questions.exp: The source uses this simplified hormonal branch to investigate passage obstruction; normal hormones alone do not prove obstruction clinically.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Which is NOT among the passage-branch examples in the source?
questions.exp: Kallmann is pretesticular. The passage branch also lists retrograde ejaculation and, controversially, varicocele.

questions.sec: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.unit: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm
questions.q: Source-check: varicocele appears under obstructive azoospermia in the diagram. Which clarification is needed?
opts: Varicocele usually causes congenital absence of both vasa and vesicles
Varicocele usually impairs testicular function, not sperm passage
Varicocele usually suppresses pituitary FSH with preserved spermatogenesis
Varicocele usually causes ejaculatory-duct obstruction with absent fructose
questions.exp: Preserve the source location while flagging the misclassification; varicocele is not a typical obstructive cause.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: Azoospermia occurs with low-volume semen and low fructose. Which contribution is deficient in the diagram?
questions.exp: Low volume and fructose suggest loss of seminal-vesicle contribution, prompting an anatomical work-up.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: The imaging step for the low-volume, low-fructose branch is ____.
questions.exp: TRUS assesses the seminal vesicles and ejaculatory pathway.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: Seminal vesicles are not seen in the low-volume branch, with suspected absent vasa. What confirms the named genetic cause?
questions.exp: The absent-vesicle/vas branch is attributed to cystic fibrosis/CFTR-related disease in the source.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: TRUS shows dilated seminal vesicles in the low-volume azoospermia work-up. Which diagnosis is shown?
questions.exp: Dilatation upstream of the distal duct suggests ejaculatory duct obstruction.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: Seminal vesicles are present and normal in the low-volume branch. Which diagnosis is suggested by the notes?
opts: Congenital absence of both seminal vesicles
questions.exp: The normal-vesicle arm points to retrograde ejaculation; postejaculatory urine can help assess it.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: Semen volume is normal and fructose is present despite azoospermia. Where does the diagram localise a block?
opts: Above the seminal vesicle, in the vas/epididymis
questions.exp: Preserved vesicle contribution favours a more proximal sperm-transport obstruction.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: The imaging test named for the normal-volume, fructose-positive branch is ____.
questions.exp: Scrotal USG follows the vas/epididymal localisation in the diagram.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: IUI deposits sperm into the ____ rather than simply into the vagina.
questions.exp: Intrauterine insemination bypasses the cervix while sperm still travel to the fallopian tube.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: The source's IUI prerequisite figures are concentration ____ and morphology ____.
questions.exp: These are the source's historical prerequisite figures, not universal modern eligibility thresholds; 14% differs from its earlier 4% morphology reference.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: Match 1) IUI-H 2) IUI-D with A) Donor semen B) Husband's semen.
questions.exp: The suffix identifies the semen source.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: The semen-processing technique labelled best in the source is ____.
questions.exp: This is the source's stated superlative, not a universal ranking for every contemporary laboratory.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.q: The volume of concentrated processed sperm injected in the illustrated IUI procedure is ____.
questions.exp: The small processed volume is placed into the uterus with an IUI catheter.

questions.sec: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique
questions.unit: Obstructive localisation and IUI technique

opts: It bypasses the cervix, but sperm must still reach the fallopian tube
It injects an embryo directly into the ovary
It bypasses both tubes by intracytoplasmic injection

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline

questions.exp: IUI still requires tubal passage; cervical and ejaculatory abnormalities can be indications.

questions.exp: IVF, ICSI, GIFT and ZIFT are listed as ART; IUI is explicitly excluded from this classification.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: The fourth ART procedure listed with IVF, ICSI and GIFT is ____.
questions.exp: Zygote intrafallopian transfer completes the list.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: A man has mild oligospermia of 12 million/mL and the partner has patent tubes. Which assisted method is listed at this level?
questions.exp: The IUI indication range is 10–16 million/mL on this page; the later management table uses 10–15.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: Match IUI indication examples: 1) Hypospadias 2) Cervical ASA 3) Vaginismus with A) Immunological cervical barrier B) Ejaculatory delivery problem C) Involuntary vaginal muscle contraction.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: IUI is performed at the time of ____.
questions.exp: Timing aims to align sperm availability with the oocyte.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline

questions.q: Source-check: a note says 'HCG is done before IUI to rule out tubal blockage'. Which correction is appropriate?
opts: Serum AMH is a radiographic patency test
HSG assesses tubal patency; hCG is an ovulation trigger
questions.exp: The handwritten abbreviation is erroneous in this sentence; distinguish HSG investigation from hCG trigger.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: Conventional IVF's sperm-count prerequisite is written as ____ million/mL in the notes.
questions.exp: This is the source's teaching threshold; actual technique selection depends on the complete semen assessment.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: Order the female IVF outline: A) Trigger B) Stimulate ovary C) TVS monitoring D) Oocyte retrieval.
questions.exp: Stimulation precedes follicle monitoring and trigger, then timed oocyte collection.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: The simplified IVF outline uses a follicle size above ____ before triggering.
questions.exp: The size criterion precedes the ovulation-trigger step.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: The male semen sample is collected on the same day as ____.
opts: Day-3 reserve testing in every case
questions.exp: The male and female branches join at same-day gamete collection and processing.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: The gamete collected for IVF is a ____ oocyte, obtained under ____ guidance.
questions.exp: The source states secondary oocyte and ultrasound-guided retrieval.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: How does conventional IVF achieve fertilisation in the outline?
opts: Sperm are placed only in the cervix
A single sperm is injected into every oocyte by definition
Processed sperm and oocyte are incubated together outside the body
Fertilisation occurs only after embryo transfer
questions.exp: Conventional IVF co-incubates gametes; direct cytoplasmic injection is ICSI.

questions.sec: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.unit: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline
questions.q: The embryo-transfer days named in the IVF overview are ____.
questions.exp: The detailed following page labels cleavage stage and blastocyst stage.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Controlled ovarian hyperstimulation is used to obtain multiple ____ for IVF.
questions.exp: The notes link multiple oocytes to embryo availability; embryo number transferred must be individualised to avoid multiple pregnancy.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The stimulation drugs named are ____ with a ____ protocol.
questions.exp: HMG/GnRH analogue is the source's stimulation regimen shorthand, not a single universal modern protocol.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Match IVF monitoring: 1) TVS 2) Blood test with A) Serum estradiol B) Follicle number and size.
questions.exp: Monitoring combines structural follicular assessment with estradiol response.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The detailed trigger criterion is at least ____ follicles measuring at least ____.
questions.exp: The detailed page adds follicle number to the 17-mm size threshold.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The trigger drug named is ____ and the notes give ovulation approximately ____ later.
questions.exp: This is the source's timing; clinical retrieval is deliberately timed before spontaneous follicular rupture.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The outline seems to place retrieval after 'ovulation occurs'. What clarification prevents losing the oocyte?
opts: Retrieval requires a menstrual bleed first
Retrieval must wait until the oocyte is in the uterus
Retrieval is scheduled after trigger but before spontaneous follicular rupture
Retrieval is performed only after implantation
questions.exp: The source's simplified arrows must not be interpreted as waiting for completed spontaneous ovulation.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Oocyte retrieval is described as ultrasound-guided, in the ____ under ____.
opts: Clinic waiting room; no sterile precautions
questions.exp: The procedural line explicitly specifies OT and anaesthesia.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Fertilisation is planned on the ____ day as oocyte retrieval.
questions.exp: The detailed IVF page states same-day fertilisation.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The culture medium is described as rich in ____, with ____ sperm per oocyte in conventional IVF.
questions.exp: Conventional co-incubation uses many sperm per oocyte, unlike ICSI's one-sperm injection.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Conventional IVF fertilisation takes place in an ____ using a ____.
questions.exp: The laboratory setting distinguishes in-vitro fertilisation from intrauterine insemination.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Match transfer stages: 1) Day 3 2) Day 5 with A) Blastocyst B) Cleavage-stage embryo.
questions.exp: The source labels day-5 blastocyst transfer better, though stage choice is patient/laboratory dependent.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The embryo-transfer target is ____ below the uterine fundus, using a ____ catheter.
questions.exp: Both position and instrument are named under embryo transfer.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Why is progesterone administered before embryo transfer in the notes?
questions.exp: Progesterone provides secretory/luteal endometrial support.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Preimplantation genetic testing is listed on embryos at day ____ or day ____.
questions.exp: The diagram proceeds to implantation if no abnormality is identified; contemporary biopsy practice commonly uses blastocysts.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The cryopreservation line specifically names the ____ oocyte.
questions.exp: Secondary oocytes can be cryopreserved; this is the gamete named in the source.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The source reports an IVF success rate of ____.
questions.exp: This is the source's reported figure, not a personal prognosis; age and treatment factors change outcomes substantially.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The source says multiple embryo transfer increases success. Which caution belongs with that statement?
opts: Multiple transfer increases multiple-gestation risk, so it is not automatically preferable
More embryos guarantee one healthy singleton
Embryo number does not affect multiple pregnancy
Multiple transfer eliminates all pregnancy complications
questions.exp: Preserve the historical source line while avoiding a blanket recommendation for multiple transfer.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Match IVF settings: 1) POI 2) Mullerian agenesis with A) Donor eggs B) Gestational surrogacy where lawful.
questions.exp: Donor oocytes address follicular failure; gestational surrogacy addresses absence of a functional uterus, subject to legal eligibility.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: Which is NOT a conventional-IVF indication in the listed group?
questions.exp: Severe oligospermia, azoospermia and marked asthenospermia are directed toward ICSI rather than conventional IVF in these notes.

questions.sec: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.unit: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications
questions.q: The listed indication that allows genetic assessment before transfer is ____.
questions.exp: Preimplantation testing is itself among the IVF indications at the bottom of the page.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: ICSI introduces ____ directly into the ____ of each oocyte.
questions.exp: Intracytoplasmic injection uses one selected sperm per oocyte; collection is otherwise described as similar to IVF.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Which is outside the page's ICSI indication trio?
opts: Mild oligospermia at 12 million/mL with adequate motility
questions.exp: The source reserves ICSI for severe count or movement problems and azoospermia with usable sperm.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: The severe motility threshold listed for ICSI is ____.
questions.exp: The threshold in the ICSI block is much lower than the reference total-motility value.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Testicular azoospermia has high FSH/LH and low testosterone. Why perform testicular biopsy in the source pathway?
opts: To confirm that normal serum FSH excludes a production defect
To find retrievable testicular sperm for possible ICSI
To establish distal duct obstruction from tissue fructose levels
To replace all endocrine and genetic assessment with morphology alone
questions.exp: If sperm are found, the diagram proceeds to surgical extraction and ICSI; diagnostic and retrieval planning require specialist judgement.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Match 1) TESA 2) TESE with A) Testicular sperm extraction B) Testicular sperm aspiration.
questions.exp: Aspiration and extraction distinguish the two testicular retrieval abbreviations.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Match 1) PESA 2) MESA with A) Microsurgical epididymal sperm aspiration B) Percutaneous epididymal sperm aspiration.
questions.exp: Both are epididymal, but percutaneous and microsurgical approaches differ.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Use the source management table: concentration is 12 million/mL, tubes are patent and other criteria fit. Which method is selected?
opts: Conventional IVF as the only option
Sildenafil solely for the sperm count
questions.exp: The table uses 10–15 million/mL for IUI; the earlier indication page uses 10–16.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Use the same management table: sperm concentration is 7 million/mL. Which method is listed?
questions.exp: Five to ten million/mL is the IVF row in this simplified treatment table.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Use the management table: sperm concentration is 3 million/mL. Which method is listed?
opts: Clomiphene alone in the female partner
questions.exp: Less than five million/mL is directed to ICSI in the source.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Non-obstructive azoospermia is managed in the table with ____ followed by ____, if sperm are obtainable.
opts: Huhner testing; IUI regardless of sperm presence
questions.exp: Successful surgical retrieval provides sperm for ICSI; retrieval is not guaranteed.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Match 1) Erectile dysfunction 2) Premature ejaculation with A) SSRI B) Sildenafil.
questions.exp: The table separates erection treatment from ejaculatory-delay treatment.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Hypospadias prevents effective semen delivery despite usable sperm. Which treatment is shown?
questions.exp: IUI bypasses the delivery problem when the partner's tubes and other prerequisites are suitable.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: In retrograde ejaculation, the table retrieves sperm from ____ for ____.
questions.exp: Sperm recovery from postejaculatory urine can permit assisted insemination after appropriate preparation.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: The two supravital stains named for distinguishing live and dead sperm are ____.
questions.exp: Eosin/trypan blue staining assesses membrane integrity, unlike the dyes used for tubal assessment.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Match supravital-stain result: 1) Stained 2) Unstained with A) Live B) Dead.
questions.exp: Dead sperm take up the stain because membrane integrity is lost.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: An immobile sperm swells in a hypotonic osmotic test. What does that indicate?
opts: It is an epithelial cell by definition
questions.exp: Swelling indicates membrane responsiveness and viability; absence of movement is not proof of death.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: In the hypotonic swelling test, no swelling is associated in the source with ____ sperm.
opts: Live but immobile in every case
questions.exp: The page contrasts no swelling/dead with swelling/live immobile sperm.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: The myeloperoxidase assay for round cells in semen is also called the ____ test.
questions.exp: Endtz helps identify peroxidase-positive leukocytes among round cells.

questions.sec: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.unit: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests
questions.q: Match source Endtz interpretation: 1) Positive 2) Negative with A) Round sperm/germ-cell interpretation B) WBC.
questions.exp: Positive supports leukocytes. The source calls negative cells round sperm without an acrosomal cap; peroxidase negativity alone is not a definitive cell diagnosis.
